newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Sallie Mae sues holder group.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sallie Mae sues holder group.

text.p: A fight between the management of Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) and an opposition shareholder group landed in federal court on Friday with the filing of a lawsuit by management.

Management and the shareholder group, known as the Committee to Restore Value (CRV), are fighting over proposals on how to change Sallie Mae from a government-sponsored enterprise to a private corporation.

"When the board approved its privatization plan, we had to file an S4 with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) which basically sets forth our business plan," said Richard Brusca, an attorney with Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher and Flom LLP, representing the management.
He said the committee, which has called a special meeting of shareholders for May 9, sent materials to shareholders that did not go through the SEC registration process.
The Sallie Mae management has scheduled its own meeting for May 15 at 1000 EDT (1400 GMT) and the special meeting sought by the committee four hours later the same day.

The committee, headed by Albert Lord, currently a director of Sallie Mae along with seven associates, has said it believed it had the right to schedule its meeting whenever it wanted and its preference was May 9.
In an interview, Brusca said he hoped Judge Harold Greene of the U.S. District Court in Washington would issue a speedy ruling before the committee's May 9 meeting date.
Brusca said initially the committee was telling shareholders a vote for its proposals would be advisory but now there was confusion about whether the proposals would be binding.
"We believe the CRV needs to file its materials and have it subject to the same review as our materials," he said. He said in effect shareholders were being asked to make an investment decision.
The suit seeks a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction until "corrective disclosure" is made, clarifying the date and the nature of the committee's meeting.
A spokesman for the committee was not immediately available.
